result.summary: DESIGN GATE: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. SCOPE: in scope (tenant-data path: binding/grant-row writers, the IdP login sync, the flag route PUT /tenant/scope-enforcement, the integrity response, audit payloads, mandatory-trigger files lib/letflow/scope_enforcement.ex flow, route authority via lib/letflow/api/scope.ex; no migration, no route reclassification, no secret resolved). The design is sound: the mode is read after lock A so the flip and every writer serialise; lock order A, T, S, then plain reads, then the audit (C) is preserved; a binding writer cannot create a tenant-wide row in on by construction; the gate refuses with every failing fact and a raise refuses; on is reached only from shadow; de-escalation is ungated; refusal audit is outside the rolled-back transaction. SEC C-1 literal check done by me: Routers.Me and Routers.Help declare GET /me/memberships, GET /me/modules and GET /help/resolved with scope: :self_service, route_scope.ex @self_service_routes lists the same three with rulings 0051-A7, SEC-518-R2-modules, SEC-518-R2-help (none pending_sec_ruling), and the 115-line snapshot has no /me or /help line: SATISFIED on main. Six required design changes (C-1..C-6 below), none large; C-1 and C-2 must be in r2 before PR 2e-a is built, C-3/C-4 before 2e-b, C-5/C-6 before 2f-a. All rulings S-1..S-10, RA-1..RA-10, OQ-1/3/4/6 in the rulings object.

rulings.S-1: SEEDING nil -> P in an on tenant: NO-ROW ACCEPTED. Basis: a binding without a grant row is denied everywhere under on (D1 fail-closed, allowed?/3 answers no_grant_rows; the coarse allow is followed by Enforce), so members of the pre-existing named group gain no capability and T9/integrity report the gap; refusing instead would halt RoleBackfill.run/0 for every later tenant (reduce_while), an availability defect with no security gain. Conditions: (a) the nested call uses the internal binding_policy option which the HTTP route can never set (scan test pins that the string occurs only in role_registry.ex, as designed); (b) the normal role_binding.created audit entry of that binding write is KEPT and its payload gains the fixed key rows = skipped_enforced so the audit shows the binding was created without a row; (c) one constant log line and the per-tenant skipped_enforced list in the report, as designed; (d) a seeded NO-ROW binding makes T9 positive, so the next flip to on is refused until an admin grants scope (test T-N3 asserts this chain). TAM nil branch / whole-tenant skip: ACCEPTED (OQ-3 too). Basis: the legacy PLATFORM_ADMIN binding and PLATFORM_ADMIN token roles are inert outside the platform tenant since REQ-447 (effective_roles drops PLATFORM_ADMIN), so skipping the removal and the token rewrite widens nothing; a bulk membership copy into the TENANT_ADMIN group in an enforced tenant would be an unreviewed tenant-wide grant. Condition: the skipped tenant is reported with rows = skipped_enforced and the mix task prints it. S-1b: see C-1; AS DESIGNED (unconditional :off for malformed prefix or missing row) is NOT accepted in production; accepted only behind a test-only configuration key.
rulings.S-1b: RULING: conditional. Analysis: (1) a tenant stored on whose row read races: the tenants row of a registered tenant always exists, a concurrent flip is serialised by lock A, and READ COMMITTED returns the committed final value after A is held, so a real race cannot yield no row; a failed read raises and the write rolls back (fail closed), which is correct. (2) attacker-influenced prefix: every prefix reaching a binding writer originates from scoped_opts[:prefix] (Plugs.Authorize via Context.scoped_repo_opts from the database-resolved tenant) or schema_name_for_tenant / the registration listing in sweeps; no body, path or query value can select it, so a malformed or unregistered prefix is not reachable by a caller, and if it were the subsequent write would address a nonexistent schema and fail. So the :off return is not exploitable today. But it is a fail-open default on a security read whose only justification is that some existing tests use hand-made schema names. Fail-open defaults on a flag read are exactly what INV-8 forbids, and the justification belongs in test configuration, not in production code. REQUIRED (C-1): production raises ModeUnavailableError for a malformed prefix and for a well-formed prefix with no tenants row; the lenient :off behaviour exists only when a test-only application key (default false/unset) is set in config/test.exs, scanned like the 518 T-D8 key (not read in config/runtime.exs, Application.get_env is the default under prod config evaluation). Alternatively, if ELIXIR-DEV proves the tests need no leniency, drop it. Either way the internal read distinguishes no-row from a row holding off, and the lenient branch emits one constant log line (no prefix).
rulings.S-2: IdP sync suppression: ACCEPTED, no-widening principle evaluated per platform role bound to the group (F4) is the right rule, the marker stamped when every candidate was suppressed (F5/RA-9) is right (otherwise lock A plus a dedup read on every login), permanent per-(user, role, action) dedup derived from stored data is consistent with 0051 N3 and accepted (R-4). Conditions: C-3 (the roles each group binds must be read AFTER lock A inside the :memberships step, not taken from the pre-lock resolve_group_ids_for_role_names result, or a concurrent rebind between resolve and lock makes the suppression test stale); would_widen? considers :platform_role bindings only (a routing-role-only group never widens, test it); a group suppressed because ANY bound role widens must not hide the non-widening roles: the audit lists only widening roles, so docs/roles.md says the whole group is withheld; the sync still never removes memberships. Suppression applies only in on (off/shadow unchanged, T-S2).
rulings.S-3: PUT authority narrowing: ACCEPTED as designed and required by decision 0051 Amendment A4 (only an interactive tenant-wide TENANT_ADMIN can flip; tokens cannot). The hoisted require_interactive_tenant_admin in Api.Scope shared with the service-principal route is right (two admin gates cannot diverge). Checked in code: handle_service_principal uses credential == :oidc (absent credential refuses), require_tenant_wide(:UsersGroupsRolesManage), TENANT_ADMIN in principal.roles and effective_scope(principal, TENANT_ADMIN) == :tenant_wide; Scope.require_tenant_wide uses allowed?/3. The platform-tenant PLATFORM_ADMIN losing the right to flip its own tenant is a deliberate narrowing and the PR body must say so; it is the safe direction (D12: turning it off is a total bypass). The narrowing also applies to off -> shadow (stage 1 allowed tokens); list that in the behaviour-change list. Condition: the :credential assign is set only by the auth pipeline (confirm at code pass) and T-H2 includes a token that carries TENANT_ADMIN. Operational finding C-4: lock-in guard for service principals.
rulings.S-4: Scoped-approver definition: AC LITERAL ACCEPTED (RA-2 default). It can only over-block (refuse a flip), never allow a lockout; the F1 exemption (a principal holding the route permission tenant-wide) is a different question and is not widened here. Active users only: ACCEPTED (inactive users cannot act; reactivation after on yields a fail-closed state because tasks carry NULL scope node, visible only to tenant-wide principals, 518 F1). OQ-4 accepted. Document that the blocker is evaluated at flip time only: a scoped approver created after on is fail-closed (cannot claim or complete) and the integrity on_gate information shows the count. If RA-2's F1-aligned predicate is adopted later, it must be exactly Scope.allowed?(principal, route_permission, :tenant_wide) being {:allow, _} (518 RA-13 condition (a)), nothing role-name based; that needs a new SEC pass.
rulings.S-5: Gate details: ACCEPTED with conditions. flush-before-flip, outside the transaction, best-effort, can only make the gate stricter: accepted. Note for the docs: the flip request itself is a counted shadow request, so the 'today has requests' day is satisfied by the flip and the every-day rule is effectively about the previous min_days dates; and request counts include every authorized request of any principal (including the flipping admin), so criterion (b) is an operator-safety control, not an adversarial one. T0 from the audit chain over both actions with after mode shadow, latest wins, fail closed when absent: accepted. configuration criterion (min_days > retention_days) names the failure: accepted. Invalid or below-floor env replaced by the DEFAULT (stricter or equal): accepted. No runtime.exs override: accepted; condition: a scan (like T-D8) asserts neither config/runtime.exs nor config/prod.exs sets :scope_shadow_min_days, :scope_shadow_min_requests or :scope_shadow_retention_days and that Application.get_env under prod config evaluation yields the defaults (test config lowers them only in config/test.exs). attrs[:now] seam: ACCEPTED, low risk. I analysed a hostile value: a future or past now cannot manufacture counter rows or a T0, and the per-day rule needs real rows for every date of the window, so the seam cannot defeat criteria (b) and (c); it can only move the duration comparison. Conditions: the router builds the flip attrs as a literal three-key map (actor_id, reason, trace_id), never from body or merged input; the scan 4.9 (4) asserts the attrs argument is that literal map and that no lib file other than scope_enforcement.ex contains the :now key in a flip call; flip/4 ignores a non-DateTime :now. No caller in production can set it.
rulings.S-6: Refusal audit best-effort, own transaction after rollback, not written for a server fault: ACCEPTED (precedent TenantAdminGuard.refuse/4 and decision 0051 D8 exception). The flip that succeeds is audited in the same transaction and a failed audit rolls the flip back, so the integrity of the on-switch trail is not best-effort. Required (C-5): the 500 path must log one constant line with the exception module only (the stage-1 flip_response drops the exception silently), so a repeated server fault is visible. shadow_required refusals are audited: accepted; an admin can create audit rows by repeated off -> on PUTs, accepted (interactive admin only).
rulings.S-7: Route census: ACCEPTED, no reclassification in 519, C-1 literal SATISFIED (verified by me, see summary), C-2 vacuous for the route table but NOT vacuous for per-PR verdicts (below). I checked the claim that no route a scoped principal reaches under on returns tenant-wide data through the default class: Enforce.check/3 sends admin_plane, tenant_wide and default-sourced routes to Scope.allowed?(principal, permission, :tenant_wide); a scoped principal is denied with the uniform 403 unless it genuinely holds the permission tenant-wide through another role (D1: then it IS tenant-wide for that permission). The skipped keys (:Unknown, :UnmatchedRoute, :UnmatchedPlatformPath, :MetricsRead) are safe: :Unknown is denied by the coarse check for every role, the unmatched keys serve no data. The three self_service routes return tenant-level or own data under rulings 0051-A7, SEC-518-R2-modules, SEC-518-R2-help whose conditions (518 R-2) still hold. Exam routes stay tenant_wide under SEC-518-R1 (walk rule exam_route_reclassified). Residual: scoped users lose definitions, entity-definition, instances and services reads (fail-closed); RA-6 follow-up required, see RA-6.
rulings.S-8: Sub-PR split with on unreachable until 2f-b: ACCEPTED (RA-5). Conditions: 2f-a must not change parse_mode/1, @modes, the transition clauses or the route (a test pins that on is still rejected after 2f-a); 2f-b merges only after 2e-a, 2e-b and 2f-a are merged with their own SEC code verdicts; the 2f-b SEC verdict is the C-1 check of record.
rulings.S-9: Accept on with no declared types and no task scope writer in production: ACCEPTED (fail-closed). It is safe because every undeclared type answers a scoped caller as no data, tasks with NULL scope node are invisible to non-tenant-wide principals, writers cannot widen, the admin plane is closed to scoped admins. It must not be sold as data-level scoping. The PR 2f-b body and docs/roles.md must say exactly the text of the runbook list in the second ruling block 'ON_IN_PRODUCTION' below. Pilot only: no production tenant is to be flipped before the RA-6 and W3b follow-ups exist, enforced by process (PR text and runbook), not by code (OQ-6 not built, accepted).
rulings.S-10: scope_delta org-unit ids in the audit payload: ACCEPTED. Same disclosure class as grant entries; readers are AuditRead holders who hold it tenant-wide (the /audit route is tenant_wide, so a scoped caller is denied); ids are record ids, no names, capped at 50 plus a count; the payload is the user's whole scope for the role, which grant entries already expose. Condition: key set asserted in tests; no org-unit names or paths in the payload.
rulings.RA-1: ACCEPTED (rows W-g1 and W-g2, scan on the six functions plus Backfill.run, indirect rows checked by T-C2). Condition: T-C2 must also assert that every INDIRECT row's entry point still reaches a scanned site (not only that the function exists), or an indirect writer that stops calling reconcile_binding! silently becomes an unclassified writer.
rulings.RA-2: ACCEPTED as default (AC literal); see S-4.
rulings.RA-3: ACCEPTED (document the platform-tenant consequence and the composed permission_scope assertion).
rulings.RA-4: ACCEPTED (Audit.list_entries has no action filter; assert the action in returned items).
rulings.RA-5: ACCEPTED. Four sub-PRs, each with its own mandatory SECURITY-REVIEWER code verdict (C-2 ruling below).
rulings.RA-6: REQUIRED, not optional: REQ-ANALYST files the follow-up requirement (rule definitions, entity definitions, services reads into :self_service one by one with a SEC ruling each, and decide instance scope T13) BEFORE PR 2f-b merges, and the 2f-b body cites its id. Without it the production value of on is unbounded-time admin-plane-only.
rulings.RA-7: ACCEPTED (one grouped counts_by_day read; counts_between unchanged).
rulings.RA-8: ACCEPTED (target-keyed pre-transaction check unchanged; the single in-transaction rule previous on and target shadow without reason is reason_required). Check ordering: the in-transaction rule must run after the same-mode short-circuit and before any write.
rulings.RA-10: ACCEPTED. Query, export and cursor pages carry no total (518 F2), which is a security property (no count oracle); the AC is read as aggregate counts and buckets plus the item set of each page. No weakening of INV-5.
rulings.OQ-1: Uniform detail enforcement_precondition_failed with codes in failed: ACCEPTED (admin-only response, counts and codes only).
rulings.OQ-3: ACCEPTED, whole TAM tenant skipped in on (see S-1).
rulings.OQ-6: Not built: ACCEPTED, provided the runbook and PR body carry the production statement of ON_IN_PRODUCTION (the process control replaces the missing signal). An informational integrity count of declaring modules may be added later without a SEC pass if it returns a number only.
rulings.C-1_ROUTE_WALK: VERIFIED BY ME on main 12a6587b7: lib/letflow/routers/me.ex has authz_get memberships (MembershipsRead) and modules (MyModulesRead) with scope: :self_service; lib/letflow/routers/help.ex has authz_get resolved (HelpRead) with scope: :self_service; Api.RouteScope @self_service_routes holds exactly these three entries with class :self_service and rulings 0051-A7, SEC-518-R2-modules, SEC-518-R2-help; none is pending_sec_ruling; test/fixtures/route_scope/tenant_wide_default_routes.txt (115 lines) contains no /me or /help line; Plugs.ApiPipeline forwards /me to Routers.Me and /help to Routers.Help only. The literal C-1 and AC 22 are satisfied. The planned test file route_scope_on_flip_blocker_test.exs (T-RW1..T-RW4) is the right guard; add to it that audit_routes/3 returns [] (already T-RW4).
rulings.C-2_PER_PR: ALL FOUR PRs are mandatory-SEC. 2e-a: tenant-data path (grant-row writers, role_registry, role_scope_grants, Backfill, TAM). 2e-b: login-path writes and audit payloads (Identity sync, membership audit). 2f-a: response shaping (integrity on_gate), new audit read, new counter read, config keys, and the OnGate/ShadowWindow code that decides the flip even though unreachable. 2f-b: the on switch (parse_mode, flip transition table, route authority, refusal HTTP mapping), mandatory trigger because it changes authorization of the flag route and touches lib/letflow/api/scope.ex (require_interactive_tenant_admin); it is also the C-1 check of record. Each PR body must contain: (1) the SEC code verdict id and status for THAT PR (a design verdict does not carry); (2) the table of routes whose class or snapshot line changed, which for all four says NONE and cites that the snapshot test/fixtures/route_scope/tenant_wide_default_routes.txt and test/support/route_inventory.ex are unchanged (git diff stat); (3) the gate output of design section 12 pasted with real results; (4) the INV-1/2/4/5/7/8 statements the diff supports. PR-specific: 2e-a: the writer registry table with the state of each row and the T-C1 scan output; the S-1 statement (NO-ROW, rows = skipped_enforced audit key); the proof that binding_policy occurs only in role_registry.ex; mix letflow.check_role_scope_grants_writers output; the statement that no tenant can reach on yet. 2e-b: the audit key sets of grant.sync_suppressed, binding.pending_scope, group_member.* scope_delta; the C-3 ordering (roles per group read after lock A); the statement that the existing export still returns User.t(); the INV-4 grep result. 2f-a: the statement that on is still unsettable and parse_mode/1 is unchanged; the list of facts and read order; the field-by-field integrity body diff; the config defaults and the T-E9 / prod-config scan; no Repo.query. 2f-b: the C-1 route walk result (this handoff's C-1_ROUTE_WALK confirmed at the PR head), the behaviour-change list (PUT narrowing for tokens and platform-tenant PLATFORM_ADMIN, also off -> shadow), the existing tests changed and why, the AC 19 decision-record amendment link or its pending status, the RA-6 follow-up id, the open follow-up for the platform-scope flip route, the ON_IN_PRODUCTION text, and the confirmation that no time-boxed 0050 D7 interim option (c) is in force (0051 Rollout 5).
rulings.ON_IN_PRODUCTION: What the 2f-b PR body, docs/roles.md and the operator runbook must say, verbatim in substance: (1) after this change a tenant that passes the gate can be set to on by an interactive tenant-wide TENANT_ADMIN, only from shadow, with an audit trail; (2) in production today on delivers: closure of the admin plane to scoped admins, a uniform 403 for scoped users on every tenant-wide route, no new tenant-wide grant rows from binding writers or IdP sync, and fail-closed grant tables; (3) on does NOT deliver data-level scoping in production: no installed module declares scope (scoped users see no entity data) and tasks have no scope node writer (scoped task workers see no tasks, scoped approvers cannot claim or complete); (4) the shadow period proves only tenant-wide and admin-plane route denials (AC 12 sentence, verbatim); request counts include the admin's own requests; (5) scoped users lose definitions, entity-definition, instance and service reads until the RA-6 follow-up ships; (6) do not scope the CANDIDATE binding (exam routes stay tenant-wide); (7) to turn on off: interactive tenant-wide TENANT_ADMIN, mandatory reason, tokens cannot; there is no platform-scope break-glass in this release (R-10); (8) pilot tenants only until RA-6 and the task scope writer exist.

required_design_changes: C-1 (2e-a, INV-8, S-1b): mode_under_lock!/1 raises ModeUnavailableError for a malformed prefix and for a well-formed prefix with no tenants row in production. The lenient :off for those two cases is available ONLY behind a test-only application key (default unset/false, set in config/test.exs only), pinned like the 518 T-D8 key: not read in config/runtime.exs or config/prod.exs, Application.get_env is the default under prod config evaluation. The internal read distinguishes no-row from a row holding off; the lenient branch logs one constant line without the prefix. Update INV-1 row, 3.2, F16, T-L1 and add a test that production-shaped config raises for both cases. If the existing tests need no leniency, the key is dropped.

C-2 (2e-a, INV-8): state that a writer whose mode read raises rolls the whole write back with the constant-detail error already used by the writer (never proceeds as off), and that Backfill.run/seeding sweeps treat a raised mode read for one tenant as that tenant's error without hiding it (report it, continue or halt as today, but never write for that tenant). Test it.

C-3 (2e-b, S-2): in 3.9 step 2, the platform roles each candidate group binds are read AFTER lock A inside the :memberships step (the tenant_roles rows with kind platform_role for the group ids), not carried from the pre-lock resolve_group_ids_for_role_names result. Add a test: a rebind of a role onto a group between the resolve and the lock does not make the suppression decision stale (use the held-lock technique of T-L2). would_widen? ignores :process_routing_role bindings (test).

C-4 (2f-a, fact 4 / OQ-5 lock-in): decide and test whether a flagged service principal (admin_flagged_service_principal) that is the only tenant-wide TENANT_ADMIN counts toward zero_tenant_wide_admins. The PUT is interactive-only, so a tenant whose only explicit admins are non-interactive principals could be flipped to on and then not be turned off through the API. Required: either exclude flagged service principals from the fact-4 count (a count variant used by OnGate only) or prove by test and document that they cannot hold the group-sourced tenant-wide TENANT_ADMIN row. Add the case to T-G4.

C-5 (2f-b, INV-8): the 500 path of flip_response (transaction_failed, audit_failed, other server faults) logs ONE constant line, e.g. scope_enforcement_flip_failed reason=<tag> exception=<module|none>, no ids, no values; test with captured log. Also confirm flip/4 rescue stays around the whole transaction including OnGate.evaluate.

C-6 (2f-b, INV-10, S-7): add a test that the PLATFORM tenant stored as on does not lock its PLATFORM_ADMIN out of the platform-scope routes (/tenants*, /onboarding*, /platform-migrations*, /event-retention*) and the flag route stays TENANT_ADMIN-only there, and one that a non-platform tenant's PLATFORM_ADMIN claim remains inert under on. Add the sentence to docs/roles.md.

C-7 (process): update section 11 and 13 with the ruling ids of this handoff (S-1..S-10, RA-6 required before 2f-b), record the per-PR verdict list of C-2_PER_PR in section 1's PR checklist, and add the ON_IN_PRODUCTION text to section 6 and 4.10.
advisories: A-1: the sync lock_timeout (2s) means a login can fail to sync under contention with a flip; it fails closed (roles empty, marker nil, next login retries). Accepted.
A-2: counters flushed by ShadowEvidence.flush/0 before the flip run inside the request process with a 30s call timeout; an admin can repeat a PUT to force flushes. Admin-only, accepted.

A-3: the integrity endpoint's on_gate evaluation without locks is labelled a snapshot; it reads token and evidence counts only and writes no audit. Tokens may read it as they may read GET / today; if that is not intended, restrict GET /integrity on_gate to interactive principals in a later change.
A-4: the fact-3 token race (token mint not serialised by lock A in all paths) is pre-existing and unchanged (R-8); accepted.

A-5: in a test sandbox Repo.in_transaction? is always true, so the inside-transaction refusal guard of BindingRefusal and RefusedAudit must be tested the way the TenantAdminGuard.refuse precedent does it, or T-R3/T-F1 will not see the entry.

A-6: sync_role_claims_from_token/3 already logs claimed_roles (IdP claim values) in a warning when no group resolves. 519 must not add claim values anywhere; consider dropping that value in 2e-b as a drive-by (INV-4 spirit, decision 0051 N3), not a blocker.
A-7: the whole-group suppression leaves no audit line for a non-widening role of a suppressed group; docs/roles.md must state that the whole group is withheld.
A-8: audit growth from repeated refusals is bounded by interactive admin traffic only; no rate limit change (decision 0040).
